summary: Provisioner migration stripped service-account-role annotation; scheduled batch workers unauthorized in private deployment
description: Issue summary: After the customer's on-prem provisioner migration to provisioner-migrate v2 (performed by their infra team on 2026-03-09), scheduled batch workers (cron-based inference jobs) began failing authorization checks against RBAC. Impact: all scheduled batch workers under tenant dataloom-prod report 403 Forbidden when attempting to access private artifact storage and inference API endpoints. Tokens are minted successfully but role bindings are missing at runtime. Customer reported >95% job failure rate for nightly pipelines.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Using private deployment in prod us-east with provisioner-migrate v2 installed
2) Provision a service account using the migrated provisioner with 'provision-job' role annotation (expected: service-account.annotation: 'redwood.role=scheduled-job-runner')
3) Trigger scheduled worker (kubectl exec into runner pod and run sample inference call)
4) Observe 403 responses from Redwood private API and 'rbac: role binding not found' in runner logs
logs: 2026-03-10T02:11:07Z runner-1 ERROR auth: authorization failed: role binding missing for principal 'svcacct:jobs/provision-job@dataloom-prod'
2026-03-10T02:11:07Z runner-1 DEBUG token: signed JWT ok, aud check passed, scopes: [inference.read, storage.read]
2026-03-10T02:11:07Z auth-provisioner WARN annotation-sanitizer: dropped unknown annotation 'redwood.role' while normalizing meta for svcacct-provision v2
investigation_notes: Initial triage: tokens and aud/sp claims look valid; failure surface is RBAC lookup returning empty bindings for the projected principal.

Hypothesis 1: Migration introduced an annotation sanitizer that strips custom annotations (redwood.role) used by downstream RBAC sync. Evidence: auth-provisioner log contains 'annotation-sanitizer: dropped unknown annotation'.

Hypothesis 2: RBAC syncer expects role mapping from service-account annotation OR a linked SCIM group. Our audit of the customer's provisioning records shows the prior provisioner wrote an explicit 'redwood.role' annotation; new provisioner writes annotation under 'x-redwood-role' (namespaced), causing lookup mismatch.
Checked RBAC DB: no role_bindings rows referencing principal 'svcacct:jobs/provision-job@dataloom-prod' (query run against private-postgres cluster at 10.2.18.7).

Reproduced in staging: replicated repro with provisioner-migrate v2 -> observed same annotation transformation and missing binding; rolling back to provisioner-migrate v1 restored role annotations and jobs succeeded.
Temporal correlation: customer performed migration 2026-03-09 23:45 UTC; failures began within 5 minutes.
comments: Support (Aisha Kumar) 2026-03-10: Acknowledged ticket and requested provisioning manifests from customer and kube-apiserver audit logs.
Customer (DataLoom Infra - michael@dataloom.com) 2026-03-10: Uploaded example manifest and cluster events. Confirmed they upgraded provisioner to v2 following vendor instructions.

SRE (Julian Park) 2026-03-11: Reproduced locally using provided manifest. Suspect annotation namespace change introduced in provisioner v2 release notes PR #412. Added link to PR in investigation notes.

Engineering (Beth Tan) 2026-03-11: Noted missing backward-compatibility shim in the provisioner for 'redwood.role' annotation. Drafted a short-term patch to copy 'x-redwood-role' -> 'redwood.role' during sync.
Customer (michael@dataloom.com) 2026-03-11: Accepted workaround and requested ETA for patch; indicated immediate business impact for overnight pipelines.
workaround: Apply temporary post-provisioning job to copy annotation key 'x-redwood-role' to 'redwood.role' on newly provisioned service accounts. Example kubectl patch script provided in comment. Alternatively, roll back provisioner to v1 if acceptable.
next_steps: 1) Engineering to backport compatibility shim into provisioner-migrate v2 (PR queued: https://github.com/redwood-inference/provisioner/pull/423)
2) Ops to coordinate hotfix deployment to affected private clusters for DataLoom (scheduled maintenance window requested by customer)
3) Support to monitor job success rates for two nights after hotfix rollout and confirm RBAC bindings created correctly
4) Follow-up postmortem to document migration checklist and update migration runbook
notes: Related runbook updated: add explicit verification step for service-account annotations after provisioner upgrades.
Customer impact: high (scheduled pipelines failure), workaround applied successfully for 60% of queued jobs during manual remediation window.
